title: Conversion of a Mobile Wallet Resend
content:
Treasury conversion rule for a **Mobile Wallet** credit sent again to the same wallet.

## What a resend carries
When a bounced credit is sent again to the same wallet at the customer's instruction, the resend carries the whole principal Paloma holds for the transfer, that is its funds-received, reversed-credit and Paloma-credit entries less its credit-sent and refund entries, as one new credit-sent entry whose credit attempt is one more than the credits already sent, and the transfer returns to processing with the release moment the moment of sending and the date available the resend day.

## Rate and amount credited
A resend converts the principal held at the transfer's locked exchange rate, and the amount it credits is that principal times that rate, rounded half up to 2 decimals.

Uplift points raise the locked rate for a resend: the uplifts are added together, the locked rate is multiplied once by one plus their sum over 100 and rounded half up to 4 decimals to give the resend rate, and the amount credited is the principal held times the resend rate, rounded half up to 2 decimals.

## Worked example (hypothetical transfer)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Funds received | 1200.00 |
| Credit sent, attempt 1 | 1200.00 |
| Reversed credit, attempt 1 | 1200.00 |
| Principal held: 1200.00 plus 1200.00 less 1200.00 | 1200.00 |
| Locked exchange rate on the transfer | 58.2150 |
| Amount credited at the locked rate: 1200.00 times 58.2150 | 69858.00 |

With uplift points of 0.20, 0.15 and 0.05 (hypothetical), the points add to 0.40; the locked rate multiplied by 1.0040 is 58.447866, rounded to 58.4479; the amount credited is 1200.00 times 58.4479, that is 70137.48. The new credit-sent entry is attempt 2.
